title: Incorporating a private limited company
law: Section 7; Rules 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 18, 23A, 25, 27, 38 and 38A of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014; Rule 8 of the Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014
summary: Register a new private company with the Central Registration Centre of the Registrar by filing SPICe+ and its linked forms, and receive the certificate of incorporation, PAN and TAN.
when: When promoters want to start a new private company.

steps.d: File SPICe+ Part A on the MCA portal with the documents and a fee of Rs. 1,000. You get two name choices and one re-submission through RUN. You may skip this and ask for name approval inside SPICe+ Part B, but do that only when you are confident the name is free.
The Registry approves or rejects the name. An approved name stays valid for 20 days from the approval date.

Draft the e-MOA (INC-33) and e-AOA (INC-34). Every subscriber signs them digitally in front of at least one witness, who also signs digitally. If there are more than seven subscribers, or any subscriber signs outside India, use paper MOA and AOA signed before a witness, using Tables A to E of Schedule I as formats.

If any object needs approval or registration from a regulator such as RBI or SEBI, get it before filing. Otherwise file a declaration with the application that the business will not start until the approval is obtained.

steps.t: Collect papers from Indian resident subscribers
steps.d: Get an INC-9 declaration (no conviction for promotion, formation or management offences, and no fraud or breach of duty finding in the last 5 years, and all filed papers are true). INC-9 is auto-generated and digitally signed in SPICe+. Also get a no-deposits declaration, PAN copy, one identity proof and one address proof. If the person already holds an updated DIN, PAN and the two proofs are not needed.
docs: Identity proof (voter ID, passport, driving licence or Aadhaar)
Address proof (mobile, telephone or electricity bill, or bank statement)

steps.t: Collect papers from foreign or NRI subscribers
steps.d: Get INC-9, a no-deposits declaration, a passport copy, a PAN copy or a declaration of no PAN, and one address proof. Authenticate all of these as Rule 13(5) requires.

steps.t: Collect papers from an Indian body corporate subscriber
steps.d: Through its authorised representative, get a copy of the board resolution authorising the subscription, INC-9, a no-deposits declaration, PAN of the body and the representative, and identity and address proof of the representative.

steps.t: Collect papers from a foreign body corporate subscriber
steps.d: Through its authorised representative, get the incorporation certificate, a declaration of no PAN, the board resolution authorising the subscription, INC-9, a no-deposits declaration, passport copy and address proof of the representative. Authenticate as Rule 13(5) requires.

Get INC-9, a no-deposits declaration, consent in DIR-2 to act as director, PAN copy, identity proof and address proof. If a director has a DIN with updated details, PAN and the two proofs are not needed.
You may give a temporary correspondence address now or the permanent registered office address. For a permanent address, keep proof of the address and utility bills not older than 2 months ready.
Prepare the AGILE-PRO form with the papers for GST, ESIC and EPFO registration. Applying for those three is optional at this stage, but filing the AGILE form with SPICe+ is compulsory.

File SPICe+ Part B with INC-33, INC-34, AGILE-PRO, INC-9 and the other papers, with fees. If the Registry finds a defect, re-submit within 15 days of its notice. A second round of 15 days is allowed. Total re-submission time cannot exceed 30 days.
When satisfied, the Registry issues the certificate of incorporation, allots DIN if you applied, and allots PAN and TAN.

If you gave a temporary address, file INC-22 within 30 days of incorporation with the registered office proof. If the company has share capital, file INC-20A within 180 days, declaring that every subscriber has paid for the shares and that office verification is filed. A practising CS, CA or cost accountant must verify INC-20A.
steps.time: INC-22 within 30 days; INC-20A within 180 days

forms.purpose: Declaration by subscribers and first directors

checklist: DSC for all subscribers, directors and witness
PAN, identity and address proofs of each subscriber
Registered office proof and recent utility bills

docs.title: Declaration on deposits (by subscriber or director)
paras: I, [name], subscriber to the Memorandum of {co} (proposed), declare that the company and its directors will not accept any deposit unless the Companies Act, 2013, the RBI Act, 1934 and the SEBI Act, 1992, and the rules and directions made under them, are first complied with and the needed filings are made with the authorities concerned.

docs.title: Authorisation by a body corporate to sign MOA and AOA
paras: RESOLVED THAT [name of authorised person], [designation], be and is hereby authorised to subscribe to the Memorandum of Association of {co} (proposed) for [number] equity shares, to sign the MOA and AOA and all forms, and to do all acts needed for the incorporation, under Rule 13 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014.
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the person so authorised is not himself or herself a subscriber to the MOA and AOA.

docs.title: Declaration for sectoral approval
paras: We declare that {co} (proposed) will not carry on the business of [activity] until it obtains the approval or registration of [name of regulator] as needed by law.
For and on behalf of the subscribers: [name], [date]

flags: The reference note gives a 6 to 73 day timeline; it adds up the stated maximums of each stage, so treat it as indicative.
The reference note does not mention payment of stamp duty on MOA and AOA, which depends on the state of the registered office; check the state rate.
The reference note says RUN allows two names and one re-submission; verify the current MCA name rules, as the name reservation process has changed over time.
Fee of Rs. 1,000 for name reservation should be verified on the MCA fee schedule.

title: Incorporating a One Person Company
law: Section 2(62) (definition of One Person Company); Section 3 (formation of company)
summary: Set up a private company with one member and one nominee by filing SPICe+ and its linked forms on the MCA portal.
when: When one individual wants to run a business through a company with a single member.
applies: One Person Company (private, limited by shares, non-government)

steps.d: File SPICe+ Part A. Choose type Private (OPC) and class One Person Company. The company must be limited by shares and non-government. Pick the NIC code for the main object. The name must end with (OPC) Private Limited. Attach the main object. Use Auto-Check for name and trademark similarity. You may submit for name reservation or go straight to incorporation.

Prepare DIR-2 consent, an NOC from the owner of the premises used as registered office, and the specimen signature of the EPFO signatory. Also collect self-attested PAN, one address proof in own name not older than 2 months (bank statement, electricity, telephone or mobile bill), one identity proof (voter ID, passport, driving licence or Aadhaar), a passport photo, and a utility bill for the correspondence or registered address not older than 2 months.

Enter authorised and subscribed share capital, the correspondence address and whether it is the registered office. If you answer No, file INC-22 within 30 days of incorporation and skip latitude and longitude. If Yes, latitude and longitude are compulsory. Attach address proof with NOC and utility bills. Pick the Registrar office by registered office location. Enter the subscriber and director count first, as the rest of the form depends on it. Fill subscriber-director details, nominee details (a nominee with a DIN is auto-filled), PAN and TAN officer codes, and the certifying professional. Stamp duty is auto-filled. Attach DIR-2 and PAN of the director and nominee. Affix DSC of subscriber-director, nominee and professional.

Use this form for GST registration within incorporation. Company name, state and district are auto-filled. Give the nature of business and the details of the director who is the authorised signatory, with email and mobile OTP checks. Attach a photo and the EPFO specimen signature. Select the police station, EPFO branch and inspection division by office address, and choose a bank. Attach identity and address proof of the signatory. The signatory's DSC is compulsory.

Company name and state are auto-filled. Give the main object in clause 3(a), exactly as in SPICe+ Part A, and ancillary objects in 3(b). Capital, subscriber and nominee details are auto-filled. Type in the subscriber's description and occupation yourself to avoid resubmission queries. Add certifying professional details. DSC of subscriber and professional are compulsory.

Company name is auto-filled. Adopt or change Table F clauses and mark any clause that does not apply as Not Applicable. Add extra clauses at point 92 (Others). The subscriber name is auto-filled but can be edited; add address, description, occupation and place to avoid queries. Add professional details. DSC of subscriber and professional are compulsory.
INC-9 is auto-filled. Verify it and affix the subscriber's DSC.
Download all forms from the Mini Dashboard tab in the MCA login, affix DSCs, upload them, and click File. Then pay MCA fees and stamp duty.
The Registry checks the forms. If it has queries, the forms come back for resubmission.
On approval, the Registry sends the certificate of incorporation, PAN, TAN letter, ESIC and EPFO details, and PTEC and PTRC details by registered mail. Master data appears on the MCA portal.
Make sure all post-incorporation filings are done within their time limits.

forms.purpose: GST, EPFO, ESIC and bank account

forms.deadline: Within 30 days of incorporation, if correspondence address is not the registered office

checklist: Name suitable and ends with (OPC) Private Limited
DSC for subscriber, nominee and professional
PAN, identity and address proofs, self-attested
Passport photo and EPFO specimen signature

docs.title: No objection certificate from property owner
paras: I, [name of owner], owner of the premises at [full address], give my no objection to the use of these premises as the registered office of {co} (proposed) from [date].

flags: The reference note says the nominee is filled in SPICe+ Part B; the nominee's written consent (INC-3) is a separate form in OPC practice. Verify how the current SPICe+ captures it.

The reference note says the name must end with (OPC) Private Limited. Check the current rule: the 2021 amendments dropped the requirement for the word (OPC) in some places; verify the current naming requirement.

The reference note says sections 98 and 100 to 111 do not apply to an OPC, which agrees with the Act; sections 96 to 99 and 101 to 111 on general meetings are generally not needed for a single member, but check section 122 and Rule 3 for the full list.
The reference note does not state the conditions on converting an OPC into another company type (the earlier paid-up capital and turnover limits were removed in 2021); verify if that is relevant.
The reference note heading for steps not applicable to private companies is not meaningful for an OPC.

title: Incorporating a Section 8 company (charitable)
law: Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013; relevant provisions of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014 and the Amendment Rules, 2015; Income Tax Act, 1961 (Sections 12AB and 80G); Central Government notifications
summary: Register a not-for-profit company, limited by shares or by guarantee, through SPICe+ and its linked e-forms.
when: When promoters want a company for charity, commerce, art, science, sport, education, research and similar aims that spends its profits on those aims.
applies: Section 8 companies, limited by shares or by guarantee

steps.d: Get promoter and director details and KYC, DIN if already allotted, registered office address and latest address proof, email and phone, a DSC for every promoter and director, authorised and subscribed capital per subscriber (for a share-capital company) or the guarantee amount per subscriber (for a guarantee company with no share capital).

File SPICe+ Part A with at most two proposed names. The names must contain words such as Foundation, Forum, Association, Federation, Chambers, Confederation, Council or Electoral Trust. You may reserve the name or proceed straight to incorporation, but do the latter only if you are sure the name is free. Optionally attach one file on the objects, the meaning and relevance of the names, and any NOC.

After name approval, open Part B from the Mini Dashboard, fill it in, affix the DSC of the proposed director by entering DIN or PAN, and upload. Attach KYC of directors without DIN, address proof with NOC and a utility bill under 2 months old, estimated income and expenditure for the next 3 financial years with sources and purpose, DIR-2, and INC-15. The remaining forms are then auto-generated.
The right table (F, G or H) is auto-filled by company type. Accept or change the clauses. Every subscriber and the professional acting as witness affix DSC, then upload.
Fill main objects in clause 3(a) and ancillary objects in 3(b). Every subscriber and the witness professional affix DSC, then upload.

Fill in the details and upload with the DSC of the director who signed SPICe+ Part B. Registration with EPFO and ESIC and a bank account application are compulsory for all new companies since 23 February 2020, and the authorities no longer issue separate numbers.
INC-9 is auto-generated from SPICe+ Part B and shows every subscriber and first director. Affix DSC and upload.
After uploading all DSC-signed forms, click File. After verification you are taken to fee payment. After payment the file goes for scrutiny.
If there is any defect, repeat the process and resubmit after correcting it. On resubmission only SPICe+ Part B and INC-35 are auto-generated. All other forms must be filled again.

forms.purpose: Declaration by subscribers and first directors

checklist: Names include a suitable word such as Foundation or Forum
DSC for every subscriber and director and the witness professional
Address proof, NOC and recent utility bill
Objects within character limits (20,000 for 3(a), 1,00,000 for 3(b))

docs.title: Note on objects and proposed names (optional attachment to SPICe+ Part A)
paras: The proposed names of {co} are [name 1] and [name 2]. The meaning of each name is [meaning].
The main objects of the company are [objects]. The names relate to these objects because [reason]. No profit will be paid to members and all income will go to the objects.

docs.title: NOC from owner of registered office
paras: I, [name of owner], owner of [address], give no objection to {co} (proposed) using these premises as its registered office from [date].

flags: The reference note does not mention INC-12 or the licence under Section 8(1). Under current SPICe+ practice the licence is issued through the incorporation package; verify whether a separate INC-12 or licence form is needed.
The reference note lists INC-13 for the MOA and INC-31 for the AOA, which fits Section 8 companies (INC-33 and INC-34 are for other companies).
The reference note says Table F, G or H applies; Table F is for companies limited by shares, G and H for guarantee companies. Verify the right table before filing.
Tax registrations (Sections 12AB and 80G) are named in governing provisions but no steps are given; plan them after incorporation.
